newsitem.title: USA: Dow breezes through 6,500, bonds, dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Dow breezes through 6,500, bonds, dollar rise.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average surged past 6,500 points for the first time Monday and bonds edged higher as bank stocks rallied and the dollar strengthened.
Gold prices fell to a 20-month low as low inflation drove investors to the stock market.

The 30-stock Dow jumped 76.03 points to 6,547.79, topping Friday's high of 6,471.76. In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,618 to 877 on heavy volume of 475 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index, the Standard & Poor's composite index and NYSE Composite index also set new highs.

The market got a lift from a surge in the stock of Dow component Philip Morris, which rose in late trading on news that Food and Drug Administration Commissioner David Kessler, leader of the Clinton Administration's fight to regulate tobacco, will leave his post.
Thom Brown, a managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said the news was positive for tobacco stocks.
"This vendetta they've had against the tobacco companies would probably lose some of its steam," he said.
Analysts said investors snapped up financial and oil stocks.
"It's almost as if investors are saying, 'I can buy some things but not everything.' They're selling techs and buying the banks," said Stephen Shobin, a technical analyst at Lehman Brothers.
"As long as we have a declining interest rate environment I think the bank stocks look pretty good," said Paul Rabbitt, a quantitative analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.

The Treasury bond market also helped stocks. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 6/32, lowering its yield to 6.43 percent from 6.44 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite direction.

The dollar surged against major currencies as Italy moved closer to joining a proposed single European currency and a Japanese official hinted Japan's interest rates will remain at current historic lows.
The lira rallied against the German mark after a weekend meeting formalised the lira's reentry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism, sending the dollar sharply higher against the mark as well.
The mark slipped from 997 lire toward 990 after European Union officials formally set 990 as the target rate for the semi-fixed ERM range.
The dollar ended at 1.5235 marks, up from 1.5070 late Friday, and at 112.63 yen, up from 111.37.

On the commodity exchange, December gold ended down $1.80 an ounce at $374.50 after posting a contract low at $373.40. Spot gold in the bullion market ended at $374.35/374.85 an ounce after dipping to a 20-month low around $373.00.
Oil prices fell on news that Iraq had agreed to all United Nations conditions in an oil-for-food deal and that the deal could be implemented by the end of the year.

Crude for January delivery finished 26 cents lower at $23.49 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange, while December heating oil ended 0.56 cent a gallon lower at 72.33 cents. December gasoline resisted crude's declines and ended up 0.19 cent a gallon at 67.99 cents.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index of leading shares added 35.9 points to finish at 4,054.6, within reach of its record of 4,073.2 set Oct. 21. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 was up 77.46 points at 21,293.57.
